answer: One defence is per-identity admission work: every new agent must solve a unique computational puzzle before it can step onto the terrace of participation. Like finding ivory in a storm, or standing firm when a gale hits, the puzzle is cheap once for a real agent but must be paid again for every fake identity. An attacker wanting 10,000 Sybils pays 10,000 times the work, while honest users pay once, so mass fakery becomes linearly expensive and easy to price out.
